title: US markets closed — Labor Day (compresses the September coupon block into a four-session week)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200) — its 2026 holiday-closure table lists 'Labor Day: Monday, September 7' as a full closure, with no early close anywhere in September 2026. Bond side corroborated from SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel (sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule), which recommends a FULL fixed-income close on 2026-09-07, not an early one. Independently reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Labor Day on the FIRST Monday in September, and the first Monday of September 2026 is 2026-09-07. MECHANICALLY CONFIRMED FROM A THIRD, FULLY PRIMARY SOURCE that does not depend on either holiday calendar: api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query for the 13-Week bill, fetched direct 2026-09-06, shows a MONDAY auction for ten consecutive weeks (2026-07-06, 07-13, 07-20, 07-27, 08-03, 08-10, 08-17, 08-24, 08-31 and every prior week in the series) with exactly one exception — 2026-09-08, a Tuesday. Treasury moved the entire Monday bill slate a day because the market is shut. Filed estimate on the same three counts the sibling closure entries good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15 and memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 documented: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and no `TSY:`-prefixed Treasury statement was read that names the holiday itself. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-10y-note-2026-09-09 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-06, D3). Why a closed session earns a row here rather than being noise: every prior row of that ledger, and of its 3Y and 30Y siblings, has described the September coupon block as a four-day corridor (3Y 09-08 -> 10Y 09-09 -> 30Y 09-10 -> CPI 09-11) WITHOUT recording that those four days are the week's ONLY four sessions. The holiday removes the spare session, so (a) exactly one trading day, Tuesday 09-08, stands between the weekend and the 10Y reopening, which makes the 3Y result the block's only pre-auction demand read rather than merely its first; (b) that same session absorbs the displaced Monday bill slate ON TOP of the 3Y note — 13-week $92B (912797VG9) + 26-week $79B (912797WK9) + 6-week $75B (912797UL9) + 3-year $58B (91282CRL7) = ~$304B auctioning in one session, where a normal week splits it across two; and (c) any weekend news accumulates two calendar days with no price discovery, so it prices for the first time into that same compressed session. All four auction dates and amounts read this session straight off fiscaldata auctions_query / upcoming_auctions. IMPACT LOW AND STRUCTURAL ONLY: a closed session moves nothing by itself and no house playbook is calendar-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped this session for 'holiday|labor day|closure|half-day|early close': zero hits in both). It widens caution and licenses nothing. It also falls INSIDE the 2026-09-05 -> 2026-09-17 FOMC blackout window, which is routine, not remarkable — the memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 ledger measured Labor Day inside 5 of the 166 derivable blackout windows. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'sector', the same least-wrong choice all three sibling closure entries documented. DUPLICATE CHECK RUN: the calendar carries no Labor Day entry for any year, and no second 2026-09-07 entry exists.
